This means that instead of researching engineering mechanisms like how to make Skills trigger automatically or how to implement nested Skill calls, teams should focus on improving the authoring ability of the Skill prompt itself. A high-quality Skill prompt requires: precise task decomposition (each Step has clear boundaries, preventing the model from getting lost between steps), explicit output expectations (telling the model what to output after each step is completed), and effective error handling (telling the model how to correct itself when common errors occur). These are essentially "prompt engineering" capabilities, not "programming" capabilities.
